_note: The GENERATED FILES: committed projections of something a human cannot diff by reading the
sources. JSON takes no comments, so this is where this file is explained.
HOW IT IS USED. L-generated regenerates every entry into a tmpdir and compares the result
BYTE FOR BYTE with the committed file. The judge and the generator are the SAME code, which
is the only arrangement in which 'the digest is current' means anything. On a mismatch the
light prints 'producer' as the CURE, so the row is actionable without reading this file.
NEITHER PRODUCER EXISTS YET, AND THE CORRECT READING OF THAT IS cannot-verify.
As of 2026-11-01 tools/gates/digest.mjs is not written and neither digest is committed
(docs/digests/ does not exist). L-generated must therefore read each entry as
cannot-verify 'producer not written: tools/gates/digest.mjs' — NOT as a fail. The difference
is the difference between 'this file is stale' and 'nothing can be said about this file',
and only the second is true today. 'producerScript' is in every entry precisely so that
state is DETECTABLE by existsSync rather than guessed at by parsing the command string.
Hard and cannot-verify blocks exactly as a fail does, so this does not make the lane green —
it makes it honest.
DETERMINISM IS A HARD REQUIREMENT ON THE PRODUCER, not a preference: no timestamp, stable
key order, no tool version in the header. A digest that differs between two runs on one tree
makes L-generated blink, and a blinking hard light gets switched off. The producer carries a
FORMAT constant instead: bumping it makes every digest stale until one --fix, so a rendering
change is one visible commit across the tree rather than a quiet drift.
ENTRY SHAPE, checked by manifestProblems() in lights/_shared.mjs:
{ "path": "<the committed file>",
"producer": "<exact command that rewrites it — printed as the cure, so it must run as written>",
"producerScript": "<the file under tools/ that must exist for the producer to run>",
"check": "<the command that only reports>",
"sourceRoots": ["<repo-relative directory the file is derived from>"],
"describes": "<one sentence: what a reader gets from the projection>" }
sourceRoots are literal directories, not globs — see visible.json for why there are no globs
in any of these manifests.

entries.describes: Every export of @cheq/core with its signature and file:line, plus the sha256 of the sources it was derived from — the surface a spec may cite and an api/web role may call, readable without opening the package.
Every route of @cheq/api: method, path, schema names, handler, file:line — the HTTP surface, which is otherwise spread across registration calls nobody can diff.
